name: Hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer

reference.source: DeVita, Hellman and Rosenberg's Cancer / NCCN genetic/familial guidelines
clinicalPearls: Caused by germline variants in the FH gene encoding the tricarboxylic acid cycle enzyme fumarate hydratase, inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern
Characterised by cutaneous leiomyomas, uterine leiomyomas (fibroids) that are often multiple and early-onset, and an aggressive form of type 2 papillary renal cell carcinoma
The associated renal cancer is prone to early metastasis even when small, so surveillance and prompt surgical intervention differ from the watchful approach used in indolent kidney tumours
Cutaneous leiomyomas presenting as firm, sometimes painful skin nodules can be the first clue and should trigger evaluation for the syndrome
Severe or early hysterectomy-requiring uterine fibroids in a family with skin leiomyomas raise suspicion
Tumours show characteristic loss of fumarate hydratase and accumulation of the oncometabolite fumarate, detectable through supportive immunohistochemistry
Because the renal tumours are aggressive, annual dedicated renal MRI surveillance and early resection are recommended
reference.pathophysiology: FH encodes fumarate hydratase, a tricarboxylic acid cycle enzyme that converts fumarate to malate. A germline loss-of-function variant followed by somatic loss of the second allele inactivates the enzyme, causing fumarate to accumulate to high intracellular concentrations. Excess fumarate inhibits alpha-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, stabilising hypoxia-inducible factors to create a pseudohypoxic, pro-angiogenic state, and also modifies cellular proteins and epigenetic marks, together promoting the smooth-muscle tumours and the aggressive papillary renal cell carcinoma that define the condition.
additionalDifferentials: Sporadic uterine fibroids or cutaneous leiomyomas
additionalInvestigations: Germline FH sequencing and deletion/duplication analysis
Annual dedicated renal MRI surveillance for early tumour detection
Dermatological examination and biopsy of suspected cutaneous leiomyomas
Tumour fumarate hydratase immunohistochemistry and staining for fumarate-related modification
Histopathological review for type 2 papillary renal cell carcinoma features
redFlags: Any solid renal mass, given the propensity for early metastasis even when small
Haematuria, flank pain or a palpable renal mass
Rapidly growing or symptomatic uterine fibroids
New or enlarging painful cutaneous nodules
reference.prognosis: Cutaneous and uterine leiomyomas are benign but can cause considerable morbidity, whereas the associated type 2 papillary renal cell carcinoma is aggressive and can metastasise early, making prognosis dependent on prompt detection. Vigilant renal surveillance with early surgery offers the best chance of cure.
pitfalls: Applying an active-surveillance size threshold suited to indolent tumours to these aggressive renal cancers
Attributing multiple cutaneous or uterine leiomyomas to sporadic disease and missing the syndrome
Delaying nephrectomy for a small renal lesion
Failing to arrange renal surveillance and cascade testing for at-risk relatives
references: DeVita, Hellman and Rosenberg's Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology
NCCN Guidelines: Kidney Cancer and Genetic/Familial High-Risk Assessment
